structured_output.status_justification: The confirmed fact set supported impact analysis across the full requested scope: all twelve phases the four Wave 1 agents own carry a recorded disposition. Two of twenty impacted modules are speculative and both carry a registered assumption and a matching risk. No open decision is blocking, so the package is neither provisional nor blocked. No identifier was renumbered and no digest changed between attempt 1 and attempt 2.

recomputed_option_ranking.method: Criterion 1, hard-constraint satisfaction, eliminates first and absolutely. Among every option, score = reuse leverage minus migration burden, where reuse leverage counts the applicable reuse-survey rows in section 7 the option satisfies by reuse-as-is or reuse-extended over that decision's declared applicable row set, and migration burden counts contract-affecting artifacts introduced that require a transition strategy. A score is recorded for every option including eliminated ones. Ties break toward the smaller impact surface, then toward the lower option identifier.

decision_D-001_output_artifact_dispositi.note: Two eliminated options outscore the selected option. Criterion 1 is applied before any score is compared, and both scores are recorded in the package so the elimination is auditable rather than hidden.

recomputed_option_ranking.selected_line_convention: Section 5.3 names exactly one option on the Selected line, `O-002`, which carries the approach's primary structural change. The composite approach's context-slice component, `O-006`, is named in the same section's Structural change item, in the 5.4 decision table, and is marked selected in its own row of the 5.2 evaluation table, so both selections remain re-derivable from the table.

validator_reconciliation.corrected_prior_self_result: 93 of 98 passed, not 98 of 98. Five agent-side checks were self-scored pass under a looser reading than the check's own decidable form.
validator_reconciliation.root_cause: Each of the five was scored against the check's intent as I had written the section, rather than against the predicate the check states. Where a check says every option is evaluated against every criterion, I accepted `n/a` as an evaluation; where it says the selection is re-derivable, I accepted two selected options against a contract that models one; where it says every contract-change module appears in the API section, I accepted the range `M-001 to M-005` as naming each; where it says every owner resolves to a known agent, I accepted a compound sentence containing an agent name; and where it says no supplied planner task is left unaddressed by the sequencing constraints, I accepted `answered elsewhere in the package` as addressed. The correction is to score each check against its predicate, not against my intent.

findings_repaired.repair: Every cell of the 5.2 evaluation table now carries an evaluation. The cross-decision constraint columns read `Not affected`, which the table defines as an evaluation recording that the option neither satisfies nor violates a constraint governing the other decision, and every option including the eliminated ones carries a score.

The Selected line names exactly one option, `O-002`, whose row the evaluation table marks Selected. The second decision's selected option `O-006` is named in the Structural change item, in the 5.4 decision table, and is marked selected in its own evaluation row, so no selection is lost.
Section 6 now names M-001, M-002, M-003, M-004, M-005, and M-006 individually, each with the cells it changes, instead of naming a range.
The Q-006 owner cell is now the bare identifier omn-tech-lead. The Producer Exclusion reasoning that made the cell compound moved to the Consequence column, where it belongs.
The Binds column now names all fifteen supplied tasks across P-001 to P-012, and the note under the table states that binding a task means constraining it, not performing it.
